facebook.content_angle: Hand entry and catch position — how a poor hand angle at entry creates immediate drag and kills propulsion before the pull even begins, and the precise fix elite swimmers use to convert every stroke into forward speed
facebook.post_text:
A bad hand entry is costing you speed before your pull even starts. 🌊

Most club swimmers enter with a dropped wrist or a wide crossover. The water slams into your forearm like a brake pad — and you've already lost the stroke.

👉 Entry angle above 45 degrees creates immediate frontal drag
👉 A crossover entry forces body rotation off-axis, killing your catch entirely
👉 Elite swimmers enter fingertips-first, thumb-side slightly down, directly in front of the shoulder — setting the catch before the pull

Fix your entry and you don't just reduce drag — you own the catch. 🔥

✔️ Aim for a fingertip-first entry, shoulder-width apart, no crossover
✔️ Extend fully forward before engaging the catch — feel the water load
✔️ Drill it at 60% pace until the pattern locks in, then bring the speed
